Heard Shri Ashish Tiwari, learned A.G.A. for the State/appellant, Shri Anil Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the accused-respondent and perused the trial court record.

2. The instant Government Appeal along with an application to grant leave to appeal has been filed by the State of U.P. against the impugned judgment and order dated 25.5.2018 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 5, Gorakhpur in Sessions Trial No. 342 of 2009 (State of U.P. Vs. Imtiyaz and others), arising out of Case Crime No. 802 of 2009, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S.-Tiwaripur, District-Gorakhpur by which the accused-respondent- Mumtaz,
brother-in-law of the deceased has been acquitted of all the charges framed against him under Section 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act.
3.

sentences.text: As per the prosecution own case as unfurled in the first information report lodged at the instance of one Shamim Ahmad uncle of the deceased Rumi on 9.6.2009, it is alleged that her real niece Rumi son of Wasim Khan was married to one Imtiyaz son of Mohd. Gani about one year back.

4. It is further alleged that Imtiyaz alongwith his father, mother and brother Mumtaz (accused-respondent) used to demand additional dowry of Rs. 50,000/-, Hero Honda motor-cycle,
colour T.V. and fridge and for non fulfillment of additional demand of dowry, they used to torture her, maltreat her and also assaulted her.
It is further alleged that ultimately in the intervening night between 8/9.6.2009, she has been done to death by setting her ablaze.
5. On the basis of said allegations, the first information report was lodged vide Case Crime No. 802 of 2009, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and  of D.P. Act, P.S. Tiwaripur, District- Gorakhpur.

After registration of the first information report, the investigation of the said case was entrusted to Mayaram Verma (P.W.-7), Circle Officer, P.S.-Kotwali, District-Gorakhpur, who recorded the statement of first informant and reached the place of incident and on the pointing out of the first informant, prepared the site-plan and recorded the statement of the witnesses Mohd. Ahmad and Waseem Akhtar.
6.

Perusal of the record further shows that the inquest was conducted on the person of the deceased by Atul Kumar Srivastava, Tehsildar, Sadar, Gorakhpur, who prepared the inquest report and thereafter prepared the relevant documents, namely chitthi R.I., chitthi C.M.O. and other relevant documents and thereafter wrapped the corpse in a cloth by preparing a sample seal and thereafter handed over the dead body to the constable for carrying it to the mortuary for post-mortem.
7. An autopsy was conducted on the person of the deceased on 10.6.2009 at 4 p.m. by Medical Officer, Dr. Ranjeet Singh (P.W.-5).

The doctor has noted the injuries on the parietal region,
occipital region and on the upper neck with haematoma present alongwith superficial deep burn and noted line of redness present on some places.
The doctor has noted cause of death to be a shock as a result of ante-mortem burn injury.

8. The Investigation Officer thereafter recorded the statement of the relevant witnesses and after collecting the relevant materials, concluded the investigation and submitted the charge-sheet against all the four accused persons, namely, Imtiyaz, Mumtaz, Smt. Mazidunnisha and Abdul Gani.

sentences.text: After committal of the case, learned trial court framed the charges under Section 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act vide order dated 4.8.2010.
An alternate charge under Section 302 IPC was also framed against the accused-respondent on 28.5.2013.
The said charges were read out and explained to the accused-respondent, who abjured the said charges, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

10. The prosecution, in order to prove the guilt against the accused-respondents, examined Shamim Ahmad (P.W.1), Parveen Khatoon (P.W.-2) is the sister of the deceased, Sajid Ali (P.W.-3) is the cousin of the deceased, Rubi Khan (P.W.-4) another sister of the deceased, Dr. Ranjeet Singh (P.W.-5) is the Medical Officer, Constable Kuber Tiwari (P.W.-6) and Investigating Officer Mayaram Verma (P.W.-7).

11. After recording the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses, the statement of accused-respondent has been recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C., in which, he has categorically stated that he is living separately on rent in the house of one Siddikur Rehman and has denied the allegations made against him.

In order to substantiate his stand of separate living,
accused-respondent Mumtaz produced one Siddikur Rehman, in whose house he used to live on rent and his testimony was recorded by the trial court as D.W.-1 and he was also cross examined by the prosecution.

12. After recording of the entire testimonies of the witnesses and hearing the accused-respondent,
the trial court though convicted the accused person Imtiyaz under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and  of D.P. Act, however finding that the prosecution has not been able to prove beyond reasonable doubt, the charges against the accused-respondent Mumtaz, who has been living separately and had absolutely no role to play in the said incident, acquitted the accused-respondent of all the charges framed against him vide judgment and order dated 25.5.2018.

13. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the said order, the present Government Appeal has been preferred by the State along with an application for grant of leave to appeal with the prayer to reverse the finding of acquittal recorded in favour of the accused-respondent and to convict him for the offences charged with.

14. Learned AGA for the State/appellant has submitted that the trial court has not appreciated the evidence and material on record in right perspective and has illegally recorded the finding of acquittal against the accused-respondent, which is bad in law and liable to be set aside.

15. Learned AGA for the appellant/State has further submitted that the finding recorded by the trial court is based on surmises and conjectures and is therefore liable to be set aside by allowing the instant Government Appeal.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the accused-respondent has submitted that accused is the brother in-law of the deceased and has absolutely no role to play in the said incident.
He infact had no concern, whatsoever with the day to day affairs between husband and wife and has been living separately in a rented house owned by Siddikur Rehman.

He further submitted that the accused being the brother in-law of the deceased, has absolutely no reason to demand additional dowry from her sister in-law and to torture her or maltreat her for non-fulfilment of additional demand of dowry.

17. Learned counsel for the accused-respondent has further submitted that general, vague and omnibus allegations has been made against the accused-respondent for demand of additional dowry, which lacks material particulars bereft of any details, rendering the complaint vague and obscure.

He further submitted that infact being the brother in-law of the deceased, he has been illegally dragged in the instant case with malafide intention only on account of his relation with the deceased husband and there is absolutely no evidence to connect him with the incident in question.

18. He further submitted that the trial court after appreciating the entire evidence and material on record by giving cogent and convincing reasons has recorded the finding of acquittal against the accused-respondent.

The view taken by the trial court is just, proper and legal and does not suffer from any infirmity or perversity and as such, the impugned order passed by the trial court do not call for any interference by this Court.

19. Having considered the rival submissions made by the parties and recapitulating the facts of the case, we find that even according to the prosecution own case, the victim Rumi was married to Imtiyaz on 17.5.2008 and used to live with her husband in a separate house alongwith his father and mother, where she is alleged to have been done to death on intervening night between 8/9.6.2009,
the information of which, was given to the family members, who reached the place of incident and finding her niece dead lodged the first information report implicating even the accused-respondent.

20. Upon going through the allegations made in the first information report as well as the statement of the prosecution witnesses, we find that there is absolutely no specific allegation of demand of dowry and consequent torture or maltreatment by the accused-respondent in connection with non-fulfillment of dowry.

Even during the course of testimony recorded by the trial court, we find that P.W.-1, P.W.-2 and P.W.-3, who are uncle, real sister and cousin of the deceased in their testimony has alleged demand of dowry in a most general, vague and omnibus manner, which lacks material particulars, bereft of any details rendering their allegations vague and obscure.
21. So far as accused-respondent is concerned, we further find that the offences charged with qua accused-respondent has not been cogently and convincingly proved by the prosecution.

Noting the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses, we find that no specific allegation regarding kind of cruelty or harassment for the non-fulfillment of demand of dowry has been recorded in their testimonies.

Furthermore, the specific date or time as to when and how the accused-respondent harassed the deceased has also not been cogently and convincingly proved by the prosecution as held by the trial court in the impugned judgement and order dated 25.5.2018, which finding, in our opinion, does not suffer from any illegality or perversity and is a possible view, which we reiterate.

sentences.text: It is further germane to point out here that the accused-respondent has taken a specific stand that he was living separately in a rented house owned by Siddikur Rehman, who has also been produced as D.W.-1.

When we go through the testimony of D.W.-1, we find that he in his examination in chief has categorically stated that Mumtaz has been living separately in a kothri (room) owned by him for the last three years from 2008 to 2011 and used to pay a rent of Rs. 200/-
for the said kothri (room).

The said witness has been put to cross examination by the prosecution,
however the prosecution could not elicit anything contrary in his statement.
He has also stated that accused-respondent Mumtaz was running a separate ready-made business in a small shop.

23. Upon going through his testimony, we do not find any reason not to come to a conclusion that D.W.-1 is a reliable witness and he in his testimony has reiterated the fact of his separate living and the prosecution could not elicit anything contrary in his statement and thus, the trial court has held him to be a truthful witness and on the basis of his testimony, has come to a rightful conclusion that the accused-respondent was living separately in a rented house and had no concern whatsoever with the day to day affairs between the husband and wife, who were living separately.

The trial court by relying upon his testimony, has rightly recorded the finding of acquittal in favour of the accused-respondent, which, in our opinion, is just, proper and legal and do not call for any interference by this Court.

24. It is further germane to point out here that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in its enumerable decisions has held that in the case of matrimonial discord between the family members, large number of frivolous complaints are filed by the family members and the wife alleging general, vague and omnibus allegations against their in laws for demand of dowry and torture as in the instant case.

25. The trial court after considering each and every aspect of the matter has passed well reasoned and detailed order holding that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove any of the charges framed against the accused-respondent.
The said finding, in our opinion, is just, proper and legal and do not suffer from any perversity and illegality and can be said to be a possible view.

26. Now coming to the scope of reversal of acquittal in Govt. Appeal, we may say that the Hon'ble Apex Court in several of its decisions has laid down the principles governing the scope of interference by the High court in an appeal filed by that state for challenging the acquittal of the accused recorded by the trial court.

This Court in the case of Rajesh Prasad Vs. State of Bihar and Another reported in (2022) 3 SCC 471 encapsulated the legal position covering the field after considering various earlier judgments and held as below: -
"29.

sentences.text: After referring to a catena of judgments, this Court culled out the following general principles regarding the powers of the appellate court while dealing with an appeal against an order of acquittal in the following words: (Chandrappa case [Chandrappa v. State of Karnataka, (2007) 4 SCC 415] "42.

entities.text: Chandrappa case [Chandrappa v. State of Karnataka, (2007) 4 SCC 415
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
From the above decisions,
in our considered view, the following general principles regarding powers of the appellate court while dealing with an appeal against an order of acquittal emerge:

sentences.text: (1) An appellate court has full power to review, reappreciate and reconsider the evidence upon which the order of acquittal is founded.

(2) The Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 puts no limitation, restriction or condition on exercise of such power and an appellate court on the evidence before it may reach its own conclusion, both on questions of fact and of law.

(3) Various expressions, such as, "substantial and compelling reasons", "good and sufficient grounds", "very strong circumstances", "distorted conclusions", "glaring mistakes", etc. are not intended to curtail extensive powers of an appellate court in an appeal against acquittal.

Such phraseologies are more in the nature of "flourishes of language" to emphasise the reluctance of an appellate court to interfere with acquittal than to curtail the power of the court to review the evidence and to come to its own conclusion.
(4) An appellate court, however, must bear in mind that in case of acquittal, there is double presumption in favour of the accused.

Firstly, the presumption of innocence is available to him under the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that every person shall be presumed to be innocent unless he is proved guilty by a competent court of law.
Secondly, the accused having secured his acquittal, the presumption of his innocence is further reinforced, reaffirmed and strengthened by the trial court.

(5) If two reasonable conclusions are possible on the basis of the evidence on record,
the appellate court should not distrub the finding of acquittal recorded by the trial court."
27.

Further, in the case of H.D. Sundara & Ors. Vs. State of Karnataka reported in (2023) 9 SCC 581,
this Court summarized the principles governing the exercise of appellate jurisdiction while dealing with an appeal against acquittal under Section 378 of CrPC as follows:-
"8.1.

entities.text: H.D. Sundara & Ors. Vs. State of Karnataka reported in (2023) 9 SCC 581
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The acquittal of the accused further strengthens the presumption of innocence;
8.2. The appellate court, while hearing an appeal against acquittal, is entitled to reappreciate the oral and documentary evidence;

8.3. The appellate court, while deciding an appeal against acquittal, after re-appreciating the evidence, is required to consider whether the view taken by the trial court is a possible view which could have been taken on the basis of the evidence on record;
8.4.
If the view taken is a possible view, the appellate court cannot overturn the order of acquittal on the ground that another view was also possible; and 8.5.

The appellate court can interfere with the order of acquittal only if it comes to a finding that the only conclusion which can be recorded on the basis of the evidence on record was State Of U.P. vs Mumtaz on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57474027/
6

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that the guilt of the accused was proved beyond a reasonable doubt and no other conclusion was possible."

29. The appellate Court, in order to interfere with the judgment of acquittal would have to record pertinent findings on the above factors, if it is inclined to reverse the judgment of acquittal rendered by the trial Court.

30. In the light of above settled proposition of law, when we go through the impugned judgment and order, we find that the trial court had given cogent and convincing reasons for recording the finding of acquittal against the accused-respondents and that the acquittal of the accused-respondents is plausible and justifiable view emanating from the discussion of the evidence available on record and does not suffer from any infirmity or perversity.
Therefore, we are of the opinion that the impugned judgment and order passed by the trial court is just, proper and legal and do not call for any interference by this Court.
31. Accordingly, prayer to grant leave to appeal is refused and the application is rejected.

Consequently, the instant government appeal is also devoid of merit and is accordingly dismissed.
32.
Let a certified copy of this judgment and order be forwarded to the court concerned for information and necessary compliance alongwith the trial court record.
